@typescript-eslint/no-require-imports.why: enabled in .oxlintrc.json but never in the production ESLint config, so it had zero parity evidence; ESLint's counterpart enabled in this probe only, in the same projectService scope as the typedSample anchor

@typescript-eslint/only-throw-error.why: typed native rule with no ESLint seatbelt coverage; the adjacent `throw new Error()` control is what proves type information reached both tools

@typescript-eslint/prefer-promise-reject.why: typed native rule production enables bare 'error'; the control rejects an Error so the row cannot be pinned by a file that always reports

@typescript-eslint/require-await.why: requires type information on the ESLint side, so it is the strongest evidence in this batch that tsgolint and projectService both resolved the file

jsdoc/check-tag-names.why: production enables it through oxlint's native jsdoc plugin with no ESLint counterpart enabled; pinned at production's bare 'error' on both sides

jsdoc/require-param.why: same native-jsdoc population; one undocumented parameter so the count is one finding rather than one per parameter
jsdoc/require-param.whyOxlintLines: oxlint's native port anchors require-param on the function declaration (line 17) while eslint-plugin-jsdoc anchors it on the JSDoc block opener (line 14); same finding, different anchor, and the count and rule both agree

jsdoc/require-param-type.why: same native-jsdoc population; the @param is present so require-param stays quiet and only the missing type reports

prefer-regex-literals.why: oxlint runs ESLint core's rule natively and reports it under the eslint(...) alias; the repo ESLint config switches the rule off while .oxlintrc.json keeps it with disallowRedundantWrapping, an option shape the probe had never exercised

arrow-body-style.why: native under the eslint(...) alias; the repo ESLint config has it off, .oxlintrc.json runs as-needed with requireReturnForObjectLiteral:false, which is what both sides are pinned to here

no-unexpected-multiline.why: native under the eslint(...) alias; the ASI hazard's merged expression still type-checks, so the control differs only by a semicolon

report-name-utils/no-function-call-in-ge.why: homemade plugin enabled in .oxlintrc.json only, scoped there to src/libs/ReportNameUtils.ts which reports nothing; the same plugin file is loaded on both sides

@dword-design/import-alias/prefer-alias.why: JS-sidecar plugin with production's alias map verbatim; the rule matches alias directories against process.cwd(), which compareFixtures.py holds identical for both tools
